title: Andhra Pradesh's New Bhogapuram Airport Launches Commercial Flights on August 17
excerpt: The Rs 5,000 crore Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport replaces Visakhapatnam's old military-shared terminal, with three airlines flying to 10 destinations including Singapore.
body:
• Air India, IndiGo, and Singapore's Scoot will operate flights from Bhogapuram to 10 destinations starting August 17, including a direct international route to Singapore.
  • The Rs 5,000 crore greenfield airport, developed by GMR Group, replaces Visakhapatnam's cramped naval base terminal and can handle 6 million passengers annually.
  • PM Modi inaugurated the airport on August 1, making it India's second new greenfield airport this year after Jewar in Uttar Pradesh.
  • A 3,800-metre runway can handle wide-body aircraft like the Boeing 777 and Airbus A330, opening the door for future long-haul routes.

The Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram in Andhra Pradesh's Vizianagaram district begins commercial flight operations on August 17, replacing the old Visakhapatnam Airport that operated as a civil enclave within the Indian Navy's INS Dega base.

Three airlines — Air India, IndiGo, and Singapore-based Scoot — will fly to 10 destinations from day one. IndiGo will operate the widest network, connecting Bhogapuram to Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai, and Tirupati. Air India will serve Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Vijayawada. Scoot's Singapore route gives the airport an international connection from launch, linking North Andhra directly to Southeast Asia's largest Indian diaspora hub.

A Rs 5,000 Crore Greenfield Airport

Developed by GMR Visakhapatnam International Airport Ltd under a public-private partnership, the airport was built on 2,200 acres about 45 kilometres from Visakhapatnam city. The first phase cost approximately Rs 5,000 crore and was completed five months ahead of schedule, according to GMR Group.

The airport's 3,800-metre Code-E runway can handle wide-body aircraft including the Boeing 777, Boeing 787 Dreamliner, Airbus A330, and Airbus A340. The 77,342-square-metre passenger terminal is equipped with biometric processing, AI-based operations, and an Airport Predictive Operations Centre. A dedicated cargo terminal with 25,000 metric tonnes of annual capacity includes temperature-controlled cold chain facilities for pharmaceuticals and marine products — key exports from North Andhra.

"We are confident that the airport will emerge as a major gateway for India's eastern corridor, driving investment, employment and regional prosperity for decades to come."

— G B S Raju, Business Chairman, GMR Airports Ltd

PM Modi Inaugurates Amid Grand Ceremony

Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the airport on August 1, accompanied by Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan, and Union Civil Aviation Minister K. Ram Mohan Naidu. Around 13,500 tribal women performed the traditional Dhimsa dance at the ceremony.

The airport is named after Alluri Sitarama Raju, a revolutionary freedom fighter from the region. Its terminal design draws inspiration from the traditional Chuttilu cottages of the Araku Valley, with a flowing form meant to evoke a flying fish. Bhogapuram is India's second greenfield airport to become operational in 2026, following Jewar airport in Uttar Pradesh, which began flights on June 15.

Replacing an Overcrowded Military Enclave

The old Visakhapatnam Airport, shared with the Indian Navy, had struggled with capacity constraints for years. The Navy stated it could not allocate additional slots for commercial flights due to increased military use of the airfield. All commercial operations will now shift entirely to Bhogapuram.

The Andhra Pradesh government invested Rs 1,583 crore in supporting infrastructure, including land acquisition, power, water supply, and approach roads. The broader integrated development spans 2,703 acres, incorporating a 500-acre aviation hub and an aviation university and EduCity on 136 acres.

What It Means for NRI Travelers

For diaspora travelers with roots in North Andhra — Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, and Srikakulam districts — Bhogapuram marks a major upgrade. The old airport's limited international capacity forced most overseas visitors to connect through Hyderabad, Chennai, or Bengaluru. Scoot's direct Singapore service offers a new routing option for those in Southeast Asia, and the wide-body-capable runway opens the door for future long-haul international connections.

The airport's initial capacity of 6 million passengers annually is designed to scale to 40 million as demand grows. GMR Group, which already operates airports at Hyderabad, Delhi, and Goa, has positioned Bhogapuram as a gateway for India's eastern corridor.
nri_angle: North Andhra NRIs gain a modern international airport with direct Singapore service, replacing the old military-shared Visakhapatnam terminal that forced overseas travelers to connect through other cities.
author: Diaspora Desk
